# Striden mot SBB och kängan mot börsens fastighetsbolag

**Feed**: borslunch  
**Published**: 2026-10-19  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

This Börslunch episode was recorded on a weak day for the Stockholm market (down more than 1%), with worries about credit and the US weighing on prices. Property advisor Sven Dahlin made a contrarian case for listed Swedish property stocks: they trade at a NAV discount of over 50%, have fallen more than 20% in a year while the market rose about 10%, rate hikes are largely priced in, insiders are buying, and companies doing the most buybacks (such as Castellum) have beaten the sector index. Credit manager Magnus Rosén said credit markets are calm despite rising government bond yields, and he leads opposition to SBB's offer for its D-shares, which he expects to fail at Friday's extraordinary general meeting.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 CAST — Castellum | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Large buybacks (~12.5% of shares, ~6bn SEK) and 20-30pp outperformance vs the sector index; sector-wide NAV discount of over 50%.

#### Reasoning

Guest Sven Dahlin (property advisor) argues for a contrarian buy of property stocks: NAV discounts over 50%, rate hikes largely priced in after a fall of more than 20%, insiders buying, and mean reversion of discounts over 30 years. Castellum is his main example of buybacks driving outperformance against the sector index. This is guest opinion, not host opinion.

#### Sell Triggers

- if buybacks stop
- if rates rise more than currently priced
- if property valuations are written down sharply

> *"Typexemplen är Castello och Maltra som har köpt in vardera ungefär 12,5 procent av aktierna och som har haft en kursutveckling som är... 20–30 procentenheter bättre än branschindex."*

---

### 🟠 BALD-B — Balder | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Alecta has bought in; part of the contrarian case on deeply discounted property stocks.

#### Reasoning

Sven Dahlin cites Alecta's purchase of Balder shares as evidence that informed investors are accumulating property stocks at large discounts. The view is only implied as part of a sector-level contrarian thesis, with no company-specific analysis.

#### Sell Triggers

- if rate rises exceed expectations
- if the NAV discount widens on write-downs

> *"Alecta har gått in i Balder."*

---

### 🟠 HUFV-A — Huvudstaden | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Love Johansson has bought into Huvudstaden; office-heavy names trade at large discounts.

#### Reasoning

Dahlin names an industry profile's purchase as a sign of insider-type buying. Office companies trade at the largest discounts, which he sees as attractive if the discounts normalise. This is a sector-level contrarian view.

#### Sell Triggers

- if office valuations fall further
- if rates rise more than priced

> *"Som Love Johansson har gått in i huvudstaden."*

---

### ⛔ CORE-B — Corem | **AVOID** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Despite buybacks by the company and by Arnhult/M2, the share price keeps falling; the only exception to buyback-driven outperformance.

#### Reasoning

Rosén and Dahlin both point out that Corem's buybacks have not lifted the share, unlike its peers. They imply the market does not trust its valuations or cash flows. This is a negative observation rather than an explicit sell call.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the share starts responding to buybacks
- if asset sales are used to cut debt

> *"Men det till trots går aktiekursen bara söderut."*

---

### 🟠 SBB-D — SBB D-aktie | **WATCH** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 60%

Guest Magnus Rosén opposes SBB's D-share offer, says holders of 33M D-shares contacted him, and expects the offer to fail at Friday's EGM.

#### Reasoning

Rosén (PAM, leading the opposition) argues the offer is unfair to D-shareholders because it drops the accrued dividend (5 SEK plus 2 SEK/yr against the 7.94 SEK offer). If the offer fails, SBB may have to pay about 800M SEK of accrued hybrid coupons before buying back D-shares on the market. The outcome is binary around Friday's EGM.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the EGM approves the offer
- if SBB does not pay the accrued coupons

> *"Men svaret på den indirekta frågan är om det här ska gå Nej, det tror jag absolut inte att det gör."*

---
